title: Blueprint node pfr_aux (PFR_conjecture_aux): fixed statement proved from eight labelled upstream nodes
intent: Freeze the statement and Lean name of the node `pfr_aux` before its proof, then prove it by composing eight already-stated upstream nodes, each cited by label and declared in one `\uses{}` line, so the proof is a linear chain of citations rather than new constructions.

parent.name: pfr_aux
parent.statement: If A ⊂ F_2^n is non-empty and |A+A| ≤ K|A|, then A can be covered by at most K^{13/2}|A|^{1/2}/|H|^{1/2} translates of a subspace H of F_2^n with |H|/|A| ∈ [K^{-11}, K^{11}] (Lean name PFR_conjecture_aux).

children.name: unif-exist
children.statement: Given a finite non-empty subset H of a set S, there exists a random variable X uniformly distributed on H.
children.closed_by: cited as \Cref{unif-exist} to obtain the uniform distribution U_A on A

children.name: uniform-entropy-II
children.statement: If X is uniformly distributed on H, then H[X] = log |H|.
children.closed_by: cited as \Cref{uniform-entropy-II} to get H[U_A] = log |A|

children.name: jensen-bound
children.statement: If X is an S-valued random variable, then H[X] ≤ log |S|.
children.closed_by: cited with U_A + U_A supported on A + A to get H[U_A + U_A] ≤ log |A + A|

children.name: ruz-dist-def
children.statement: Ruzsa distance d[X;Y] := H[X' - Y'] - H[X']/2 - H[Y']/2 for independent copies X', Y'.
children.closed_by: applied to turn the doubling bound into d[U_A;U_A] ≤ log K, and again at eq. (uauh) to rewrite d[U_A;U_H] as an entropy bound

children.name: entropy-pfr
children.statement: For G = F_2^n and G-valued X^0_1, X^0_2, there is a subgroup H ≤ G with d[X^0_1;U_H] + d[X^0_2;U_H] ≤ 11 d[X^0_1;X^0_2].
children.closed_by: applied with X^0_1 = X^0_2 = U_A to obtain the subspace H with d[U_A;U_H] ≤ (1/2)C' log K, C' = 11

children.name: ruzsa-diff
children.statement: If X, Y are G-valued random variables, then |H[X] - H[Y]| ≤ 2 d[X;Y].
children.closed_by: gives |log |H| - log |A|| ≤ C' log K, closing eq. (ah)

children.name: bound-conc
children.statement: If X is an S-valued random variable, then there exists s ∈ S with P[X = s] ≥ exp(-H[X]).
children.closed_by: gives the point x_0 with the concentration lower bound on U_A - U_H

children.name: ruz-cov
children.statement: If A, B are finite non-empty subsets of a group G, then A can be covered by at most |A + B|/|B| translates of B - B.
children.closed_by: covers A by translates of (A ∩ (H + x_0)) - (A ∩ (H + x_0)) ⊆ H, closing the covering bound

applicability.goal_shape: A covering/transfer theorem whose hypotheses are about a set A (non-empty, doubling |A+A| ≤ K|A|) and whose conclusion quantifies over a witness H (existence of a subspace with a size bound), proved by a linear chain of citations to already-stated nodes.
applicability.use_when: the result is a known combination of already-proved (or already-stated) lemmas; the proof is a sequence in which each step invokes exactly one upstream node; the statement can be frozen, with its Lean name and `\leanok`, before the proof is written.
applicability.avoid_when: the proof needs a new construction or a new lemma that must itself be stated and proved (that belongs as its own node in the graph); the statement may still change (then do not fix the Lean name yet); or the hypotheses of the cited lemmas do not line up into a single chain.

claims.claim: The proof of pfr_aux (lines 24-47) cites exactly the eight labels declared in \uses{...} on line 25 — nine \Cref{} calls, with ruz-dist-def cited twice — and ends with 'This proves the claim' without introducing any new node.
The statement and its Lean name are fixed before the proof and both are marked checked: the lemma carries \lean{PFR_conjecture_aux}\leanok on line 15 and the proof carries \leanok on line 25.

consequences: Freezing the statement first means the Lean name PFR_conjecture_aux must correspond to a provable Lean statement; if the statement later changes, the name and the \lean{} marker change with it. The proof carries the obligation that each cited node's hypotheses are discharged in the state where it is invoked (for example entropy-pfr is applied only after ruz-dist-def has turned the doubling bound into d[U_A;U_A] ≤ log K). A citation whose hypotheses do not line up leaves a silent gap, because the blueprint's \leanok is a claim the build verifies, not something the text itself enforces.
